body.html:
Strategy · site auto-deployment · Barkpark Cloud vs Vercel

The two loops — where we actually stand against Vercel on auto-deploy

A code-verified gap analysis of Barkpark Cloud's hosted-site deployment against Vercel. The honest frame: there are two auto-deploy loops. Vercel owns the git loop (push → build → preview URL → merge → production) — ours is missing three links, verified in source. We own the content loop (Studio publish → debounced rebuild → live) — which Vercel can only approximate with webhook glue. The roadmap below closes our missing links first, then weaponizes the loop only we have.

1 · The two loops

Vercel's entire product gravity sits in the git loop; their content story is "add a CMS webhook to a Deploy Hook." Our gravity is inverted: the content loop is live in production and recently tuned (signed content-publish webhook → Oban-debounced rebuild, bursts collapse to one trailing build), while the git loop is honest scaffolding. Neither company has the other's loop. That symmetry is the strategic map.

2 · Our git loop today — verified against source, not the brochure

Link in the chainState todayEvidence
Inbound push webhookWorks. HMAC-verified (constant-time), branch-routed, honest responses in GitHub's delivery log.router.ex:5554, 9678
Production-branch push → buildDoes not build — by design honesty. github_build_available? is hard-coded false; the push mints a *born-failed* deployment whose reason says: github push builds require the GitHub App (not yet available) — deploy an artifact via bp deploy.router.ex:9775, 9769
Fetching the pushed codeDoes not exist anywhere. No git clone, no tarball fetch — not on the box, not in the control plane. Even the GitHub App client seam has no archive/clone call. A push delivers a sha we cannot turn into bytes.github/real.ex (seam), grep across cloud/+internal/+deploy/
Branch push → previewBuilds — the wrong code. A real preview deployment is minted and served (dedicated Caddy block, cert-on-demand, per-branch replace, branch-delete teardown) but it builds on-box template source + bound dataset content, not the pushed commit. It is a content preview wearing a code-preview costume.router.ex:9870, registry.ex:4380
Preview public DNSUnresolved. Preview hosts route only if a request already reaches the box; no public A record. DNS is owned by the Go warm-pool path, unreachable from the webhook path. Two options documented, none chosen.cloud/TODO-gh-6-preview-dns.md
Status back to GitHubNone. No commit statuses, no check runs, no PR comment. The only feedback is the webhook HTTP response.GitHub.Client behaviour (no such callback)
GitHub App seamBuilt, dark. JWT + installation tokens + create-repo + push-files + auto-register-webhook all implemented behind a config gate; 503s until GITHUB_APP_ID+GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY are wired (the gh-1 human gate). Manual paste-the-webhook link path works without it.github/real.ex, runtime.exs:146, router.ex:5386/5451
The three missing links
(1) Source fetch — add tarball/archive download to the App seam and teach the box builder to unpack it as SITE_SRC keyed by sha. (2) The gate — wire the App credentials and flip github_build_available?. (3) Feedback — post commit status / check run + one PR comment carrying the preview URL. Until all three exist, "like Vercel" is not a polish problem — the loop is open-circuit.

3 · Feature-by-feature against Vercel

DimensionVercelBarkpark Cloud todayVerdict
Git integrationGitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket Apps, zero-config import, private repos via installation tokensApp seam built but dark; manual webhook paste; public-repo assumptionsGap (wave 1)

Rollback / promoteInstant alias flip on immutable deployments; Rolling Releases (canary %); skew protectionBlue/green with health gate; instant symlink/port-flip rollback (static/node); promote-by-new-deployment (container)Parity in spirit — our rollback story is genuinely good
Build skip / change detectionIgnored-build-step; skips unaffected monorepo projectsbuild_id = hash(code+content+config) exists but a no-change push still buildsCheap win — we already compute the key; just skip + say "unchanged"
Deploy hooks (URL triggers)First-class per-branch hook URLsContent-publish webhook is effectively one, hardwired to content eventsCheap win — generalize
Env varsPer-environment (prod/preview/dev + custom), per-branch overrides, pull to localOne encrypted write-only blob per siteGap (wave 2) — preview env inherits prod today
Build observabilityStreaming logs, deploy summary, checksLive stage ladder + streaming console + honest failure copy — arguably more honest than Vercel'sParity+

Data locality at buildBuild fleet fetches the CMS over the public internetBuilder and content share the box — dataset reads at build time are loopbackWe lead (structural, not copyable)
Edge / CDNGlobal edge network, ISR, image optimizationOne named box + optional Cloudflare proxied mode (cf_proxied) as the edge storyContrast, not gap — see §4
Compute modelFluid compute, functions, middleware, queues, cronA real server you own; scale_mode always_on / zeroContrast — deliberately different product
Cost & sovereigntyAbstracted infra, usage pricingNamed Hetzner/Azure box, price shown before charge, archive → resurrect, adopt/eject, BYO providerWe lead for our audience
Deploy governanceRBAC, protection rules, conformance (enterprise)Team RBAC + append-only audit + canary autoupdate brake (for the *platform*, not yet per-site)Mixed — enough for now

4 · Contrasts — differences that are identity, not deficit

• Named box vs anonymous fleet. A Barkpark site runs on a server the customer can see, price, archive, resurrect, even eject and keep. Vercel's abstraction is the opposite bet. We should never blur this to look more like them — it is the reason to choose us.
• Price before charge. The provisioning theater shows €/month before anything bills. Vercel bills usage after the fact. Keep the contrast loud.
• Honesty as UI. Our born-failed deployment with a humanized reason, "unmetered" meters, and failure-beats-false-green are a *stricter* honesty regime than Vercel's. The gap analysis must not sand this off while chasing parity.
• Content and site co-located. Their build fleet treats the CMS as a remote API; our builder reads the dataset over loopback. Structural advantage: content-rev-addressed builds (build_id already hashes content_rev) — Vercel cannot name a deployment by its content state.
• One box is not a CDN. True, and fine: cf_proxied mode is the edge story for sites that need it. We sell sovereignty-with-an-edge-option, not edge-with-a-sovereignty-story.

5 · What we're missing — ranked

Wave 1 — close the git loop (the "like Vercel" moment)

1. Wire the GitHub App (gh-1, human gate: create the App, set GITHUB_APP_ID/GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY). Everything below hangs off it.
2. Source fetch: add get_archive(repo, sha) to the GitHub.Client seam (tarball endpoint, installation-token auth), stream to the box as sha-keyed SITE_SRC; teach site-deploy.sh to build from it. Private repos come free via installation tokens.
3. Flip `github_build_available?` from constant to "App configured + repo linked via App" — production pushes then mint real queued deployments.
4. Make previews truthful: preview builds use the pushed sha's source (same fetch path). Until then previews are mislabeled content previews.
5. Preview public DNS (gh-6): decide wildcard-per-instance vs control-plane DNS seam; wildcard *.{instance}.barkpark.cloud A record at provision time is the cheaper call and needs no CP→DNS coupling.
6. Status + PR comment: post a check run per deployment (queued/building/live/failed with the honest failure sentence) and one PR comment with the preview URL. This single feature is most of what makes Vercel *feel* magic.

Wave 2 — DX ladder

1. Skip-unchanged builds: build_id already exists — short-circuit identical hashes, record a "skipped · unchanged" deployment state (new vocab value, worth it).
2. Generic deploy hooks: mint per-site trigger URLs (the content webhook generalized beyond content events).
3. Repo import picker: list_repos already exists in the seam — a /new-style import flow (pick repo → detect framework → create site → auto-webhook).
4. Framework auto-detection on import (package.json/astro.config sniffing) instead of a manual field.
5. Per-environment env: split the env blob into production/preview scopes (keep write-only semantics per scope).
6. Preview protection: at minimum a per-site password/token wall on preview hosts (they will leak URLs).
7. Build cache: persist npm/astro caches per site on the box between builds — trivially available since builds are stateful-box-local; Vercel had to engineer remote caching, we get it for free.

Wave 3 — weaponize the loop they don't have

1. Draft-content previews: preview = pushed branch's code × draft dataset content. Vercel needs bespoke CMS preview-mode integrations for this; for us it is a query flag on a loopback read. This is the feature to market, not parity.
2. Content-rev pinned deploys: expose "this deployment = code sha X × content rev Y" in the ladder and allow re-deploying either axis independently.
3. Publish-gated deploys: optional "hold site rebuilds until N publishes settle" — editorial batching Vercel cannot express.

6 · Anti-goals — Vercel features we deliberately do not chase

• Serverless/Fluid functions, edge middleware, queues, cron-as-product — our compute story is the box itself; adding a FaaS would blur the one clear contrast we have.
• Global build fleet / remote build caching — box-local caches capture most of the value at zero architecture.
• Marketplace, AI Gateway, analytics products — out of scope for the hosting surface; Plausible env vars already ride the templates.
• Image-optimization CDN — revisit only if template sites demonstrably suffer; cf_proxied absorbs much of it.

7 · Sequencing note

Wave 1 is one epic: five of its six items are pure engineering behind the single human gate of registering the GitHub App (item 1). The born-failed scaffolding, the App seam, preview routing, cert-on-demand, and the build_id discipline mean the loop was designed to be closed — the remaining work is the tarball fetch, the DNS decision, and the check-run client. Recommend running it as a bp-epic-cycle wave once the App is registered; wave 2/3 items become its verified backlog.

Code-verified 2026-07-18 (router.ex, github/real.ex, sites/deploy.ex, box_relay.ex, site-deploy.sh, TODO-gh-6-preview-dns.md). Companion papers: designer handover · design phase closed.

body_html:
Strategy · site auto-deployment · Barkpark Cloud vs Vercel

The two loops — where we actually stand against Vercel on auto-deploy

A code-verified gap analysis of Barkpark Cloud's hosted-site deployment against Vercel. The honest frame: there are two auto-deploy loops. Vercel owns the git loop (push → build → preview URL → merge → production) — ours is missing three links, verified in source. We own the content loop (Studio publish → debounced rebuild → live) — which Vercel can only approximate with webhook glue. The roadmap below closes our missing links first, then weaponizes the loop only we have.

1 · The two loops

Vercel's entire product gravity sits in the git loop; their content story is "add a CMS webhook to a Deploy Hook." Our gravity is inverted: the content loop is live in production and recently tuned (signed content-publish webhook → Oban-debounced rebuild, bursts collapse to one trailing build), while the git loop is honest scaffolding. Neither company has the other's loop. That symmetry is the strategic map.

2 · Our git loop today — verified against source, not the brochure

Link in the chainState todayEvidence
Inbound push webhookWorks. HMAC-verified (constant-time), branch-routed, honest responses in GitHub's delivery log.router.ex:5554, 9678
Production-branch push → buildDoes not build — by design honesty. github_build_available? is hard-coded false; the push mints a *born-failed* deployment whose reason says: github push builds require the GitHub App (not yet available) — deploy an artifact via bp deploy.router.ex:9775, 9769
Fetching the pushed codeDoes not exist anywhere. No git clone, no tarball fetch — not on the box, not in the control plane. Even the GitHub App client seam has no archive/clone call. A push delivers a sha we cannot turn into bytes.github/real.ex (seam), grep across cloud/+internal/+deploy/
Branch push → previewBuilds — the wrong code. A real preview deployment is minted and served (dedicated Caddy block, cert-on-demand, per-branch replace, branch-delete teardown) but it builds on-box template source + bound dataset content, not the pushed commit. It is a content preview wearing a code-preview costume.router.ex:9870, registry.ex:4380
Preview public DNSUnresolved. Preview hosts route only if a request already reaches the box; no public A record. DNS is owned by the Go warm-pool path, unreachable from the webhook path. Two options documented, none chosen.cloud/TODO-gh-6-preview-dns.md
Status back to GitHubNone. No commit statuses, no check runs, no PR comment. The only feedback is the webhook HTTP response.GitHub.Client behaviour (no such callback)
GitHub App seamBuilt, dark. JWT + installation tokens + create-repo + push-files + auto-register-webhook all implemented behind a config gate; 503s until GITHUB_APP_ID+GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY are wired (the gh-1 human gate). Manual paste-the-webhook link path works without it.github/real.ex, runtime.exs:146, router.ex:5386/5451
The three missing links (1) Source fetch — add tarball/archive download to the App seam and teach the box builder to unpack it as SITE_SRC keyed by sha. (2) The gate — wire the App credentials and flip github_build_available?. (3) Feedback — post commit status / check run + one PR comment carrying the preview URL. Until all three exist, "like Vercel" is not a polish problem — the loop is open-circuit.

3 · Feature-by-feature against Vercel

DimensionVercelBarkpark Cloud todayVerdict
Git integrationGitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket Apps, zero-config import, private repos via installation tokensApp seam built but dark; manual webhook paste; public-repo assumptionsGap (wave 1)
Push → production buildEvery push builds; managed build fleet; framework auto-detect (40+)Born-failed row + honest advice; framework is a manual fieldGap (wave 1)
Preview deploymentsImmutable unique URL per push, PR comment, deployment protection (SSO/password)Per-branch preview, replace-per-branch, cert-on-demand, live console — wrong source code, no public DNS, no protection, no PR linkHalf-built (wave 1)
Rollback / promoteInstant alias flip on immutable deployments; Rolling Releases (canary %); skew protectionBlue/green with health gate; instant symlink/port-flip rollback (static/node); promote-by-new-deployment (container)Parity in spirit — our rollback story is genuinely good
Build skip / change detectionIgnored-build-step; skips unaffected monorepo projectsbuild_id = hash(code+content+config) exists but a no-change push still buildsCheap win — we already compute the key; just skip + say "unchanged"
Deploy hooks (URL triggers)First-class per-branch hook URLsContent-publish webhook is effectively one, hardwired to content eventsCheap win — generalize
Env varsPer-environment (prod/preview/dev + custom), per-branch overrides, pull to localOne encrypted write-only blob per siteGap (wave 2) — preview env inherits prod today
Build observabilityStreaming logs, deploy summary, checksLive stage ladder + streaming console + honest failure copy — arguably more honest than Vercel'sParity+
Content → deployWebhook glue to a Deploy Hook; preview mode requires CMS integration workNative: publish → signed webhook → debounced rebuild; provenance recorded (content-auto vs manual)We lead — this is the loop they don't have
Data locality at buildBuild fleet fetches the CMS over the public internetBuilder and content share the box — dataset reads at build time are loopbackWe lead (structural, not copyable)
Edge / CDNGlobal edge network, ISR, image optimizationOne named box + optional Cloudflare proxied mode (cf_proxied) as the edge storyContrast, not gap — see §4
Compute modelFluid compute, functions, middleware, queues, cronA real server you own; scale_mode always_on / zeroContrast — deliberately different product
Cost & sovereigntyAbstracted infra, usage pricingNamed Hetzner/Azure box, price shown before charge, archive → resurrect, adopt/eject, BYO providerWe lead for our audience
Deploy governanceRBAC, protection rules, conformance (enterprise)Team RBAC + append-only audit + canary autoupdate brake (for the *platform*, not yet per-site)Mixed — enough for now

4 · Contrasts — differences that are identity, not deficit

  • Named box vs anonymous fleet. A Barkpark site runs on a server the customer can see, price, archive, resurrect, even eject and keep. Vercel's abstraction is the opposite bet. We should never blur this to look more like them — it is the reason to choose us.
  • Price before charge. The provisioning theater shows €/month before anything bills. Vercel bills usage after the fact. Keep the contrast loud.
  • Honesty as UI. Our born-failed deployment with a humanized reason, "unmetered" meters, and failure-beats-false-green are a *stricter* honesty regime than Vercel's. The gap analysis must not sand this off while chasing parity.
  • Content and site co-located. Their build fleet treats the CMS as a remote API; our builder reads the dataset over loopback. Structural advantage: content-rev-addressed builds (build_id already hashes content_rev) — Vercel cannot name a deployment by its content state.
  • One box is not a CDN. True, and fine: cf_proxied mode is the edge story for sites that need it. We sell sovereignty-with-an-edge-option, not edge-with-a-sovereignty-story.

5 · What we're missing — ranked

Wave 1 — close the git loop (the "like Vercel" moment)

  1. Wire the GitHub App (gh-1, human gate: create the App, set GITHUB_APP_ID/GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY). Everything below hangs off it.
  2. Source fetch: add get_archive(repo, sha) to the GitHub.Client seam (tarball endpoint, installation-token auth), stream to the box as sha-keyed SITE_SRC; teach site-deploy.sh to build from it. Private repos come free via installation tokens.
  3. Flip `github_build_available?` from constant to "App configured + repo linked via App" — production pushes then mint real queued deployments.
  4. Make previews truthful: preview builds use the pushed sha's source (same fetch path). Until then previews are mislabeled content previews.
  5. Preview public DNS (gh-6): decide wildcard-per-instance vs control-plane DNS seam; wildcard *.{instance}.barkpark.cloud A record at provision time is the cheaper call and needs no CP→DNS coupling.
  6. Status + PR comment: post a check run per deployment (queued/building/live/failed with the honest failure sentence) and one PR comment with the preview URL. This single feature is most of what makes Vercel *feel* magic.

Wave 2 — DX ladder

  1. Skip-unchanged builds: build_id already exists — short-circuit identical hashes, record a "skipped · unchanged" deployment state (new vocab value, worth it).
  2. Generic deploy hooks: mint per-site trigger URLs (the content webhook generalized beyond content events).
  3. Repo import picker: list_repos already exists in the seam — a /new-style import flow (pick repo → detect framework → create site → auto-webhook).
  4. Framework auto-detection on import (package.json/astro.config sniffing) instead of a manual field.
  5. Per-environment env: split the env blob into production/preview scopes (keep write-only semantics per scope).
  6. Preview protection: at minimum a per-site password/token wall on preview hosts (they will leak URLs).
  7. Build cache: persist npm/astro caches per site on the box between builds — trivially available since builds are stateful-box-local; Vercel had to engineer remote caching, we get it for free.

Wave 3 — weaponize the loop they don't have

  1. Draft-content previews: preview = pushed branch's code × draft dataset content. Vercel needs bespoke CMS preview-mode integrations for this; for us it is a query flag on a loopback read. This is the feature to market, not parity.
  2. Content-rev pinned deploys: expose "this deployment = code sha X × content rev Y" in the ladder and allow re-deploying either axis independently.
  3. Publish-gated deploys: optional "hold site rebuilds until N publishes settle" — editorial batching Vercel cannot express.

6 · Anti-goals — Vercel features we deliberately do not chase

  • Serverless/Fluid functions, edge middleware, queues, cron-as-product — our compute story is the box itself; adding a FaaS would blur the one clear contrast we have.
  • Global build fleet / remote build caching — box-local caches capture most of the value at zero architecture.
  • Marketplace, AI Gateway, analytics products — out of scope for the hosting surface; Plausible env vars already ride the templates.
  • Image-optimization CDN — revisit only if template sites demonstrably suffer; cf_proxied absorbs much of it.

7 · Sequencing note

Wave 1 is one epic: five of its six items are pure engineering behind the single human gate of registering the GitHub App (item 1). The born-failed scaffolding, the App seam, preview routing, cert-on-demand, and the build_id discipline mean the loop was designed to be closed — the remaining work is the tarball fetch, the DNS decision, and the check-run client. Recommend running it as a bp-epic-cycle wave once the App is registered; wave 2/3 items become its verified backlog.

§
